subject: Energy
title: Thin-Film Solar Cells
description: A quick win: understand Thin-Film Solar Cells.

hook.text: Thin-film cells use layers just 1–2 micrometers thick—hundred times thinner than silicon wafers.

buildup.text: Materials like cadmium telluride (CdTe) and CIGS are deposited on glass or flexible substrates.

discovery.text: Thin-film uses far less material—and can be made flexible, lightweight, and integrated into building surfaces.

twist.text: CdTe panels by First Solar are the cheapest to manufacture—but cadmium is toxic, raising disposal concerns.

climax.text: Thin-film holds about 5% of the market—niche but valuable for applications where silicon is too heavy or rigid.

punchline.text: Thinner than hair—flexible solar for any surface.
